The thesis

Electric should never mean apologetic.

The AURA One is not a quiet commuter pretending to be a motorcycle. It is a ground-up electric platform built around a centre-mounted liquid-cooled motor, a structural battery, and a chassis tuned at the Anglesey circuit. The result is a machine that out-accelerates a litre superbike to 60 and still carries you 171 miles between charges.

Powertrain

One motor. Centred. Liquid-cooled.

Rather than bolting a hub motor to the rear wheel, we mounted a 110 kW oil-cooled axial-flux motor at the centre of mass. Mass sits low and central, so the AURA One turns in like a 600 and holds peak torque from a standstill to 80 mph without thermal roll-off.

  • Axial-flux motor, 110 kW peak / 65 kW continuous
  • 408 lb-ft at the crank, available from 0 rpm
  • Sealed wet clutch for true engine-braking feel
  • Sustains peak output for 90s laps without derating

Engineered around the ride

Details that disappear.

Adaptive haptic suspension

Semi-active damping reads the road 500 times a second and firms up under braking. Three rider-selectable maps, infinitely tunable in the app.

Edge-to-edge HUD

A 7-inch bonded glass display with optically-laminated anti-glare. Turn-by-turn, charge-aware routing, and a circuit telemetry mode.

AuraDock fast charging

10–80% in 38 minutes on a 7 kW AuraDock, or top up overnight on any wall outlet. CCS adapter available for public DC networks.
